When ring A rises until the line connecting it with the fixed pulley is in a horizontal position, its rising speed v1≠0. If at this time the speed of B is v2, then (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, ring A sleeved on a vertical thin rod is connected to weight B by an inextensible light rope passing over a fixed pulley. Since the mass of B is relatively large, after B is released, A will rise along the rod. When ring A rises until the line connecting it with the fixed pulley is in a horizontal position, its rising speed v1≠0. At this time, what is the speed v2 of weight B equal to?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a vertical thin rod, and ring A is sleeved on the thin rod; at the upper right there is a fixed pulley; a light rope extends obliquely upward from ring A to the fixed pulley, then passes around the fixed pulley and vertically downward connects to weight B. The figure also draws a horizontal dashed line passing through the fixed pulley, used to indicate that when A rises to the same height as the fixed pulley, the line from A to the fixed pulley is horizontal. Reasoning: Let the horizontal distance from the fixed pulley to the vertical rod be the constant x, and let the vertical height difference between A and the fixed pulley be y, then the length of this segment of rope from A to the fixed pulley is l=√(x^2+y^2). Let the vertical rope length on the B side be s. The rope is inextensible, so l+s=constant. Differentiating with respect to time gives dl/dt+ds/dt=0, where dl/dt=(y/√(x^2+y^2))·dy/dt. When A is at the same height as the fixed pulley, y=0. Even if at this time the rising speed of A is dy/dt=v1≠0, there is still dl/dt=0. Therefore ds/dt=0. The magnitude of the speed of weight B is just the magnitude of the rate of change of the vertical rope length on the B side, so v2=0.
